All-Inclusive Resort

Coral Lagoon Resort & Spa

By Marcus Webb · April 2, 2026 · Updated August 10, 2026

Best for families with toddlers and preschoolers who want a calm, low-effort all-inclusive week.

Coral Lagoon Resort & Spa is an all-inclusive property built around a single idea: a calm, shallow lagoon pool that works for the youngest kids in the group without boring everyone else. It won’t suit families chasing dramatic beaches or nightlife, but for a low-effort week with toddlers or preschoolers, it’s one of the more thoughtfully designed resorts we’ve reviewed in the region.

Room options

Family Suite

Two queen beds plus a pull-out sofa, sleeps up to 5. The practical default for most families of four.

Swim-Up Suite

Ground-floor rooms with a private step straight into a quiet pool section — worth the upgrade with kids under 6.

Two-Bedroom Villa

A separate lounge and kitchenette, best for multigenerational trips or two families travelling together.

Kids facilities

  • Supervised kids club, split by age group, 9am–9pm
  • Splash pad and shallow lagoon pool section for under-5s
  • Family-style buffet with a dedicated kids' station at every meal
  • In-room crib and baby-monitor rental available on request

Activities

  • Snorkeling trip to a nearby reef (best for kids 7+)
  • Evening family show in the main plaza most nights
  • Optional day trip to Xcaret, about 40 minutes away

Nearby attractions

Tulum ruins

About an hour's drive — doable as a half-day trip if your kids can handle some walking in the heat.

Xcaret eco-park

A full-day outing with underground rivers and wildlife exhibits; popular enough that early arrival matters.

Pros and cons

What we liked

  • Shallow, gently sloped lagoon pool that toddlers can actually use safely
  • Kids club staff genuinely engaged, not just supervising screens
  • Swim-up suites mean nap times don't end the pool day

Worth knowing

  • Main buffet gets loud and crowded 6–7:30pm — early dinner avoids it
  • Beach itself is narrow; the lagoon pool is the real draw, not the sand
  • Wi-Fi is patchy outside the main lobby

Frequently asked questions

Is Coral Lagoon Resort good for toddlers?

Yes — it's one of the better options in the area specifically because of the shallow lagoon pool and swim-up suites, both of which matter more for toddlers than the beach itself.

Is it worth booking a swim-up suite?

If you have a child under 6 who naps, yes — being able to step straight into the pool during nap-adjacent hours changes the rhythm of the day noticeably.
